definition: Rows of the same kind of thing, scanned down a column. The row carries every state — the table around it is a border, a radius and a clip.
reachForItWhen: The user compares one field down a column — which of twelve renders finished, which one failed.
Every record has the same columns and the same types, and the row count is unknown until runtime.
The user picks several records now and acts on all of them afterwards.
A record's name, its state and a quantity have to be readable in one horizontal pass.

reachForSomethingElseWhen.situation: The records have different shapes — one carries a thumbnail, another three lines of prose.
reachForSomethingElseWhen.instead: Card. A column holding a paragraph in one row and `0:12` in the next is not comparable down its length, and the grid is then decoration.

reachForSomethingElseWhen.situation: There are three records and no column anyone compares down.
reachForSomethingElseWhen.instead: Card, or a stack of them. A three-row table is a grid drawn around nothing.

reachForSomethingElseWhen.situation: Clicking a record navigates away and the view changes.
reachForSomethingElseWhen.instead: Card with `interactive`, which renders a real `<button>` and carries the affordance. A `<tr>` carries none: the row is for a selection that persists in place, not for departure.

reachForSomethingElseWhen.situation: The rows have not arrived from the network yet.
reachForSomethingElseWhen.instead: Skeleton, shaped like the rows. A rendered table with empty cells claims the rows exist and are blank.

reachForSomethingElseWhen.situation: There is one record and the fields are different kinds of thing — a name, a prompt, a resolution, a seed.
reachForSomethingElseWhen.instead: Card with a definition list inside it. A two-column label/value table borrows table semantics for a layout, and a screen reader then announces "column 2 of 2" over every value the user wanted.

variants.useWhen: Every `<tr>` in `<tbody>`, without exception — one variant covers all of them, and the recipe lists it first, so it is also the default. A row you want to draw attention to is the selected state, not a third variant.
variants.avoidWhen: Never on the `<thead>` row: `row` binds hover and a focus ring, so a header built from it lights up under the pointer and takes a tabstop that activates nothing.

variants.useWhen: The one `<tr>` in `<thead>`, once per table. It binds base only and declares `focus: 'none'` — the statement that a column label is not a control.
variants.avoidWhen: Never as a group separator inside `<tbody>`, and never as the thing a sort click hangs on: `FOCUS_CLASSES.none` is the empty string, so a sortable `<th>` built this way is keyboard-dead. Put a ghost Button inside the cell, which brings its own ring and its own 44px target.

guidance.useWhen: Every table. It is the only size the recipe declares, and `sizeClasses.md` is the empty string — the geometry lives in `cellClasses`, so a second size could vary nothing but padding.

sizes.note: A data cell is `py-space-3` on a 14px `body sm` line box: 8 + 20 + 8 = 36px, from `--oz-space-3: 8px`, `--oz-text-body-sm: 14px` and `--oz-leading-body-sm: 1.4286` in `dist/tokens.css`. A header cell is the same padding on a 10px `label xs` box at leading 1.2, so 28px. Between them sits the divider: `border-b-2` resolves through `dist/tailwind.tokens.js` to `--oz-stroke-2`, which is 1px, not Tailwind's ordinal 2px. 36px clears SC 2.5.8's 24×24 CSS px and sits 8px under this system's own `--oz-target-min` of 44px. Where the row is the only path to the record on touch, the edit is `py-space-3` → `py-space-4` in `cellClasses` and lands on exactly 44px — one edit, every table. Padding added at a call site gives two tables that disagree about how tall a row is.

copy: **Column header copy:**
write in sentence case — `Clip`, `Model`, `Status`, `Length`; `headerCellClasses` carries `uppercase`, and a DOM string already in capitals is spelled out letter by letter by some screen readers
name the field and leave the unit in the cell — `Length`, never `Length (mm:ss)`
keep to one or two words at 10px — `Model` and `Status` fit; `Estimated render duration` sets a column width nothing else in the table needs
say what the thing is, not what the field is called — `Clip`, never `Name` and never `ID`

leave the header empty for a column of row actions — the `<th>` still carries `scope="col"`, so the column keeps its binding to its cells and loses only its name, and a screen reader walking the header row hears nothing there; `Delete permanently` on the control below already says what the cell does, and `Actions` announces a noun ahead of it once per row
pick a visible word or nothing — `Column.label` is typed `string` and `headerCellClasses` carries no `sr-only`, so a visually hidden column name is not expressible at all
**Cell copy:**

put the record's own identifier in column one — `street-dusk-01`, never `Row 1` and never a sequence number; `Table.tsx` gives cell index 0 `font-medium text-content-primary` whatever it holds, so a duration parked there gets the emphasis of a name and the table stops being scannable by name
write status as a word the user repeats back to support — `Ready`, `Rendering`, `Failed`
use one em dash where a value does not exist yet — `—`, never `N/A`, never `null` and never an empty cell, because an empty cell is indistinguishable from a rendering bug
keep the unit attached to the number — `0:12`, not `12` under a header that has to explain it
move anything needing a sentence to the record's detail view — a cell that wraps to three lines has stopped being comparable down its column
right-align a column of quantities with `Column.align` — `0:12` and `0:08` then line up on the colon and `—` lands where the eye already is
**Caption copy:**
name what the rows are and which ones — `Recent renders`, never `Table` and never `Results`
write one on every table; it renders `sr-only`, so it costs nothing on screen and it is the only accessible name the table has
keep it to a noun phrase under six words — it is announced ahead of the row and column counts
say the filter when one is applied — `Renders from the last 7 days` tells a screen-reader user why a clip they expected is absent
**Empty-state copy** (rendered instead of the table, not inside it)**:**
say what would be here and how to get one — `No renders yet`, then `Describe a shot above and Seedance 2 will return four variations in about a minute.`
put the action in it — `Generate your first clip`, as a primary Button
reject `No data`, `Nothing to show` and `0 results` — none of the three says whether the user filtered the rows away or the account is new
motion: A table is scanned, and the pointer crosses rows while the eye reads down a column. Only the row's background changes, and it settles before the pointer reaches the next row. Rows do not arrive individually; twenty staggering in is decoration over the thing people came to read. No press, deliberately: a row that dips under the cursor moves the click target during the click. B16's grading has nothing to collapse here — nothing in a row travels.

behaviourUnderPressure.case: A cell value longer than its column
behaviourUnderPressure.behaviour: It wraps and the row grows taller; no cell sets `white-space: nowrap`, so nothing is cut. `.oz-truncate` on a `<td>` is a defect rather than a fallback — the table is `w-full border-collapse` at `table-layout: auto`, so the cell sizes itself from its content, the ellipsis never renders, and the `nowrap` the class brings with it pushes the table into the wrapper's clip. Add `.oz-break` where the value has no break opportunity at all: `harbour-pan-04-take-12-final-v3`, a hash, a path.

behaviourUnderPressure.case: More columns than the container is wide
behaviourUnderPressure.behaviour: Column widths are content-driven, so they redistribute down to min-content and then the table overflows the wrapper — whose `overflow: hidden`, there to keep row fills inside the 12px radius, eats the rightmost column with no scrollbar and nothing on screen saying a column is missing. The policy is scroll: wrap the component in `.oz-reel`, B17's guard for this case. Its children are non-shrinking flex items (`flex: 0 0 auto`), so the wrapper takes the table's own width instead of being narrower than it, and the guard is written in logical properties (`overscroll-behavior-inline`) so the scroll axis follows the writing direction.

The container does not grow while the columns' min-content roughly doubles, so a table that fitted at 100% reaches the same clip at 200% and loses its right-hand column silently. WCAG 1.4.4 requires 200% with no loss of content, and nothing in this repo measures a rendered table width — this is a manual pass at 200%, in the narrowest container the table ships in.

Render the empty state instead of the table. A `` with no `` leaves a 28px header band on its 1px divider with nothing beneath it, which reads as a failed fetch rather than an empty account. `Assembled.tsx` swaps the whole table for `rounded-6 border-2 border-dashed border-border-secondary bg-surface-primary p-space-11`, carrying `No renders yet`, one line and a primary Button. No component owns that panel — it is a `
`, a `

` and a Button.

behaviourUnderPressure.case: The user tabs to a row that is already selected
behaviourUnderPressure.behaviour: No focus ring appears. `Table.tsx` renders a selected row through `Recipe.classes({ force: 'selected' })`, and the forced branch returns before `FOCUS_CLASSES` is appended: the compiled string is exactly `bg-fill-selected text-content-primary`, with no `focus-visible:outline`, no `hover:` binding and no transition. `onRowClick` still gives the row a tabstop, so it is focusable and unmarked while focused, and the `aria-selected:` classes the recipe compiles are dead in this component. Check it by tabbing through a table with a row already selected.

The table widens toward the scroll case rather than squeezing its neighbours to nothing. A long header — `Wiedergabelänge` under a 10px `label xs` — claims its own column's width first, and the columns that lose space stop at min-content. Test the German build inside the narrowest container the table ships in, not at a narrow window; the two are different failures.

enforced.claim: The header pairing clears 4.5:1 in both modes — `content/tertiary` on `surface/secondary` measures 5.61:1 light and 6.86:1 dark.

Every foreground/background pair these two variants create is measured in both modes, with translucent tokens flattened first. The table's four are row base 13.90:1 / 11.17:1, row hover 17.35:1 / 14.08:1, row selected 17.26:1 / 15.36:1, header 5.61:1 / 6.86:1.
enforced.assertion: `showcase/scripts/verify-contrast.ts`, run by `npm run verify` in `showcase/`. The 2026-08-02 run reports 9 components and 98 pairings — wcag 70, apca 28 — all clearing their floors.

enforced.claim: A colour-only transition cannot be given an overshooting spring, and the spring it does get does not overshoot.
enforced.assertion: `ComponentRecipe.motionConsistent` in `showcase/lib/core/Recipe.ts`, swept by `showcase/scripts/verify-motion.ts`; the emitted curve is measured by `MOTION_ASSERTIONS` in `build/spec.mjs` — overshoot 0, `reports/audit.json`.

enforced.claim: Both dividers stay visible, at different floors. The header divider is `border/primary`, gated against the page and against `surface/primary` — 1.30:1 and 1.20:1 light, 2.49:1 and 2.27:1 dark, against a 1.1 floor. The row divider is `border/tertiary`, gated against `surface/primary` alone at a 1.6 floor — 1.67:1 light, 4.33:1 dark.
In dark mode a floating surface sits above `surface/tertiary`, so a table dropped into a dialog or popover lands on a rung of its own rather than on the one its header row already occupies.
enforced.assertion: `SURFACE_LADDER` in `build/spec.mjs` — ΔL 0.0433 for `surface/elevated` over `surface/tertiary` against a 0.03 floor (`reports/audit.json`).

enforced.claim: There is one size, and a second is not expressible without editing the recipe.
The cell-to-column association cannot be dropped at a call site.
enforced.assertion: `Table.tsx` writes `scope="col"` on every `<th>`; the `Column` type has no field for it, so a caller can neither omit nor override it.

enforced.claim: A caption goes on every table.
enforced.assertion: Convention only. `caption` is optional in `TableProps` and nothing in `build/` or `showcase/scripts/` measures an accessible name — a table without one renders, typechecks and passes `npm run verify`. Review step.

notEnforced: That the row divider survives the row hover it separates. `COLLISION_ASSERTIONS` holds `border/primary` apart from `fill/tertiary-hover` — the bridge's `--accent`, the pair that actually shipped equal — and that is the wrong token on both sides of this table. The divider between two data rows is `border/tertiary`, and this table's hover is `fill/primary-hover`: the pair measures 1.553:1 in light and 3.842:1 in dark, which is ample, and `border/tertiary` is named against no fill anywhere in the list. CLAUDE.md rule 4 is exactly this shape of gap.

That the header divider is visible on the surface a dialog puts the table on. `VISIBILITY_ASSERTIONS` names `border/primary` against `surface/primary` and `background` only. On dark `surface/elevated` that same border measures 1.455:1 — computed with `contrast()` from `build/palette.mjs`, by no gate.

That the row divider is visible against the page. `VISIBILITY_ASSERTIONS` names one pair for `border/tertiary`, against `surface/primary`, and a table dropped straight onto the page has `background` behind its rows because the row base is `transparent`. That pair measures 1.813:1 light and 4.736:1 dark, and on dark `surface/elevated` 2.772:1 — all computed with `contrast()`, none of them gated. The header divider is gated against the page and the row divider is not, which is rule 4 inside one family of three.

Any table pairing on a surface other than the page. `verify-contrast.ts` flattens translucent tokens over `background` before measuring, so the selected tint is measured over the page and never over the dialog. `content/primary` on the selected tint over dark `surface/elevated` measures 8.96:1, computed by hand with `composite()` and `contrast()`.

That selection is legible without colour. `fill/selected` over the page measures 1.173:1 light and 1.130:1 dark against SC 1.4.11's 3:1 for a state indicator — and the hovered row and the selected row differ by 1.005:1 in light, L* 94.7 against L* 94.8. In greyscale they are the same row, which is SC 1.4.1. This is what a Checkbox column is for: `aria-selected` carries selection for a screen reader, the tick carries it for everyone reading on a dim panel, in greyscale, or across a room.

That a selected row keeps its focus ring. Nothing asserts that `Recipe.classes` with `force` still emits a focus class, and `verify-classes.mjs` cannot see it — that script reports classes present in the prerendered HTML with no matching CSS rule, and this is a class absent from the HTML.

That `aria-sort` is set on a sorted column. `Table.tsx` writes `scope` and nothing else on the `<th>`; `TableProps` carries no sort state and no gate expects one, so a sorted table announces its sort to nobody.

That a `text-right` column right-aligns for the reason you think. `cellClasses` ships `text-left` and `Table.tsx` appends `text-right`; `cx` does no conflict resolution, so stylesheet order decides — `.text-right` lands 58 bytes after `.text-left` in the compiled sheet and wins there, not in the class attribute.
That `.oz-truncate` is absent from every `<td>`. It compiles, renders no ellipsis, and pushes the table into the clip.

That a table which can outgrow its container is wrapped in `.oz-reel`. `Table.tsx` renders its own wrapper and cannot see the container; `Assembled.tsx` ships the table in `.oz-enter-rise` with no reel, correct for that column and wrong in a 200px one.

That `forceRowState` stays in the showcase. It renders a state with no pseudo-class behind it — a row that permanently looks hovered and never responds to being hovered. `Table.tsx` marks it "Showcase-only, as elsewhere" and nothing in `npm run verify` tells showcase code from product code.

looksLikeABugButIsNot.observation: A hovered row is exactly the header's colour.
looksLikeABugButIsNot.why: `fill/primary-hover` and `surface/secondary` are byte-identical in both modes — `#EFEDEC` light, `#211F1D` dark, `dist/tokens.css`. Hovering the first data row matches it to the header at 1.000:1, and the whole boundary is the 1px `border/primary` beneath the header, at 1.117:1 light and 2.017:1 dark. Both are the same rung of one ramp, which is why the divider is structure rather than decoration.

looksLikeABugButIsNot.observation: In dark mode a table inside a dialog has a header band darker than the dialog, and its rows darken on hover.
looksLikeABugButIsNot.why: `surface/secondary` names a rung, not a relative tint, so it does not track what it floats on. On dark `surface/elevated` (`#393735` since B18) the header reads at 1.386:1 below the surface. Before B18 that same header and that same hover measured 1.000:1 against `surface/elevated` and were invisible. Darker-than-the-surface is the new behaviour and it is the one you can see.

looksLikeABugButIsNot.observation: The last row has no bottom divider.
looksLikeABugButIsNot.why: `Table.tsx` writes `border-b-2` on cells where `i < rows.length - 1`. A trailing divider would draw a straight 1px line 1px inside a 12px corner radius, where it cannot follow the curve and the clip takes its last 12px at each end — and it would draw it in a second token a pixel from the first. The divider is `border/tertiary` (`#C2C0BF` light, `#7C7A78` dark); the wrapper is `border/secondary` (`#CCC9C8`, `#5F5D5C`). They sit 1.101:1 apart in light, which reads as one edge drawn twice at the wrong weight, and 1.532:1 apart in dark, which reads as two. The wrapper's edge is the table's last line.

looksLikeABugButIsNot.observation: A focused row's ring is trimmed at the table's left and right edges.
looksLikeABugButIsNot.why: The ring is an outline at a 2px offset (`--oz-focus-ring-width`, `--oz-focus-ring-offset`, both 2px), and the wrapper's `overflow: hidden` clips to its padding box. The table is `w-full`, so the outline's vertical strokes fall outside that box, and the first and last rows lose their outer horizontal stroke too. The clip is not removable — it is what keeps row fills inside the 12px radius.

related.difference: When the records stop having the same shape, the comparison is gone and the grid is decoration. Card's decision is which rung of the surface ladder it sits on; a table's rows name no surface at all — the row base is `transparent` — so a table inherits whatever it is dropped onto, and its figures change with it.

When the selection is the thing the user is building — twelve clips to delete together — the tick is the record of it. Checkbox also owns the mixed state a select-all header needs, which `selectedKeys` on its own cannot express.

When a cell holds a status word — `Ready`, `Rendering`, `Failed` — it holds a Badge: the row supplies the record and the Badge supplies the state, at `size="sm"` with `dot`, which is what `Assembled.tsx` ships in the Status column.

When the rows have not arrived, the loading shape replaces the table. Skeleton is `aria-hidden` with the live region on the group, so the announcement is "Loading recent renders" rather than eleven unlabelled boxes.

When each row carries a setting the user writes immediately, the cell holds a Switch and the row is scaffolding. Selection is `aria-selected` and reverts with the view; a toggle writes on change and survives it.

When the screen's action is the point — `Generate video` above the table, `Generate your first clip` inside the empty state — the Button owns the primary. At most one primary per view, so a column of per-row primaries spends it once per record.

changed.what: 2026-08-02 — dark `surface/elevated` and `surface/overlay` moved to `neutral/105` (`#393735`, L* 33.8). Every figure on this page for a table inside a dialog, a popover or an `overlay` Card is new.
changed.why: B18. Both floating surfaces were `neutral/120` and `neutral/115` and sat below `surface/tertiary`. `#211F1D` is also `surface/secondary` and `fill/primary-hover`, so a table on a dark floating surface had a header band at 1.000:1 against it and a row hover that changed nothing at all. Both now measure 1.386:1.

changed.what: 2026-08-02 — the header divider on a dark floating surface is weaker than it was: `border/primary` against `surface/elevated` measures 1.455:1, down from 2.017:1.
changed.why: B18 raised the surface and `VISIBILITY_ASSERTIONS` names only `surface/primary` and `background`, so this pair is measured by no gate. Recompute it before deepening a table's dividers on a dialog rather than carrying the old figure across.

changed.what: 2026-08-02 — contrast gates went 118 to 130, and six of the new pairs are `content/*` on `surface/elevated` and `surface/overlay`.
changed.why: B18b. Those two surfaces were the only places text could be set with no floor at all; raising the ladder put a floor under all three content roles there, and the tightest pair the addition created is `content/tertiary` in dark at 4.95:1 against 4.5 — the pair that sets the ceiling on how light a dark surface may be (`reports/audit.json`). A table's cell text inside a dialog is now gated where it was not.

B18c. No binding in `table.recipe.ts` names a disabled fill — the row binds base, hover and selected, the header binds base. Recorded so a reader diffing `dist/tokens.css` does not go hunting for a table consequence.

changed.what: 2026-08-02 — B19 routed the press-scale through `--oz-motion-spatial-scale`. No table changes.
changed.why: `tableRecipe.motion` declares no press, so `motionClasses` emits `transition-colors` and its spring pair and no transform at all. Recorded because B19 is marked M in DECISIONS.md and a reader auditing `Recipe.motionClasses` will land here.

changed.what: 2026-08-02 — this page previously called `border-2` a 2px border, five times, and rested its divider argument on that weight. It is 1px.
changed.why: `dist/tailwind.tokens.js` maps `borderWidth.2` to `--oz-stroke-2`, which `dist/tokens.css` sets to 1px — the ordinal stroke scale is remapped, so Tailwind's ordinal meaning does not survive the preset. Every wrapper and divider figure here was recomputed against the emitted files. CLAUDE.md rule 5.
